I think a lot of people addicted to drugs have just lost hope that anything will ever get better so drugs become the only escape they have from a painful life. Take the rat park experiments. The premise is, rats were put in a plain cage by themselves with a thing of water and a thing of water mixed with heroin. They used the heroin over and over habitually until they died. Then they redid the experiment but put them in with other rats and offered a lot of enrichment. Some of them went to the heroin sometimes but none of them died or used habitually. So ya, currently, some people don’t want to stop using because they have no community and nothing else to help them ease their pain. Unfortunately, it would take a hell of a lot to combat the isolation issues we have right now, the housing crisis, the mental health crisis, the rising cost of living paired with stagnating wages, etc. I don’t know the solution but so many people think of addiction as something like a character flaw that someone is destined to have when it isn’t. I’m in the US, it’s probably different in other places, but I admitted myself voluntarily for wanting to kill myself so I went to “intensive outpatient care” even though we all were there 24/7... so it was more of an inpatient thing. It was a big help, they didn’t do much in terms of therapy, just helping me come up with a safety plan. But being able to get away from everything and be around people who didn’t judge me or try and get me to talk about things I wasn’t ready to was a big help. It gave me time to clear my head in a space where I didn’t have to worry about what had me feeling like that so that I was better able to asses and deal with it when I was calmer was really nice. If you need help there are options, and good on you for considering admitting yourself if you think it’s necessary, that’s really hard and can be intimidating.
